state.misconception_label: Thinks you can find missing values in a given table by treating the row as linear and adding on the difference between the first two values given.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: The equation \( f=3 r^{2}+3 \) is used to find values in the table below. What is the value covered by the star? \begin{tabular}{|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline\( r \) & \( 1 \) & \( 2 \) & \( 3 \) & \( 4 \) \\ \hline\( f \) & \( 6 \) & \( 15 \) & \( \color{gold}\bigstar \) & \\ \hline \end{tabular}. I got \( 24 \) because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher

score.justification_pass1: The teacher uses vague metaphors rather than directly addressing the linear-addition misconception, but the student does successfully move from their incorrect method to correctly applying the quadratic equation by the end.
score.justification_pass2: While the teacher attempts to use a real-world analogy (map with coordinates), it remains abstract and doesn't connect to concrete everyday experiences, failing to ground the mathematical concept in a tangible situation students would encounter.
